ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two MOS transistors connected in series vertically, labeled T1 and T2. The upper terminal of T1 is connected to +5 V, and the gate of T1 is also connected to its upper terminal through the left-side connection; the lower terminal of T1 is connected to the upper terminal of T2, and this middle node is labeled as output Vo. The gate of T2 is connected to this middle node through the left-side connection, and the lower terminal of T2 is grounded. Therefore according to the figure one can take VGS1 = 5 - Vo, VGS2 = Vo. Reasoning: The problem gives the threshold voltage of the two transistors VT = 1 V, K1 = 36 μA/V^2, K2 = 9 μA/V^2. The two diode-connected transistors are in series, and the DC currents are equal, so K1(VGS1 - VT)^2 = K2(VGS2 - VT)^2. Substituting gives 36[(5 - Vo) - 1]^2 = 9[Vo - 1]^2, namely 36(4 - Vo)^2 = 9(Vo - 1)^2. In the effective conduction region Vo < 4 and Vo > 1 are required, so take the positive overdrive branch: 6(4 - Vo) = 3(Vo - 1), equivalent to 2(4 - Vo) = Vo - 1. Solving gives 8 - 2Vo = Vo - 1, 3Vo = 9, so Vo = 3 V.

method.method_draft: From the figure, define overdrives Vov1 = VGS1 - VT = (5 - Vo) - 1 and Vov2 = VGS2 - VT = Vo - 1. The two devices are in series, so their currents are equal. With K1/K2 = 36/9 = 4, equal current gives Vov1/Vov2 = sqrt(9/36) = 1/2. The total voltage from +5 V to ground is the sum of two thresholds plus two overdrives: 5 = 1 + Vov1 + 1 + Vov2, hence Vov1 + Vov2 = 3. With Vov1:Vov2 = 1:2, get Vov2 = 2 V, so Vo = VT + Vov2 = 1 + 2 = 3 V.
